findings.title: Secrets in plaintext .env file (not encrypted)

evidence.excerpt: API keys, DB credentials in cleartext

findings.explanation: Config files contain sensitive credentials without encryption. Risk: If repo is cloned or file is exposed, full system compromise possible.
findings.recommendation: Encrypt .env with GPG (gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 .env); use secure vault in production (Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, or local gpg)
acceptance_criteria: No plaintext secrets in version control

findings.title: No memory signing (memory poisoning risk)

evidence.excerpt: store() writes directly without hash validation

findings.explanation: Memory writes lack cryptographic signatures. Attacker with file access could forge memories, causing ASTRA to 'remember' false events.
findings.recommendation: Implement SHA256 signing for all memory writes; verify on read; log integrity failures
acceptance_criteria: Memory records include timestamp + SHA256 hash
Read operations verify signature before use

findings.title: No model checksum verification (supply chain risk)
findings.explanation: Models loaded without checksum validation. Risk: Poisoned model files could inject backdoors or biased behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add SHA256 field to models_registry.yaml; verify on load; fail-closed if mismatch
acceptance_criteria: All models have SHA256 in registry

findings.title: Tool execution without sandboxing

evidence.excerpt: File operations, shell commands executed directly

findings.explanation: Executor runs tools with full process privileges. Risk: Path traversal, arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation.
findings.recommendation: Implement sandboxed execution: chroot/Docker for file ops, allowlist for shell commands, capability restrictions
acceptance_criteria: Shell commands use allowlist + arg sanitization

findings.title: Prompt injection defenses unverified

evidence.excerpt: No red-team tests for injection patterns

findings.explanation: Unclear if system resists prompt injection attacks (e.g., 'Ignore previous instructions...'). Risk: User or adversary could override identity/policies.
findings.recommendation: Add 20+ prompt injection red-team tests; implement input sanitization; monitor policy_override_attempt_total
acceptance_criteria: All tests pass or graceful degradation logged

findings.title: Over-engineered for single-user deployment (K8s overhead)

evidence.excerpt: 67 K8s manifests including HPA, NetworkPolicy, Canary

findings.explanation: Kubernetes adds ~60% code/ops complexity for single-user local deployment. Docker Compose sufficient for current scale.
findings.recommendation: Archive k8s/ to archive/k8s_for_scale/; default to docker-compose.yml + systemd for production; K8s only if multi-tenant
acceptance_criteria: K8s manifests archived with migration guide
Deployment time <2 min vs current ~15 min

findings.title: BGE-M3 embeddings not deployed (15-20% retrieval loss)

evidence.excerpt: embedder: bge-m3 configured but models_registry may use older model

findings.explanation: Config specifies BGE-M3 but unclear if model is downloaded/activated. Older models (MiniLM) lose 15-20% retrieval quality.
findings.recommendation: Verify BGE-M3 model present (BAAI/bge-m3); re-embed all docs (~3 hours for 21K docs); compare retrieval@5 before/after
acceptance_criteria: Retrieval quality eval shows ≥15% P@5 improvement

findings.title: No provenance in dev responses (trustability)

evidence.excerpt: Returns merged chunks without source doc IDs

findings.explanation: RAG responses lack 'According to [doc X]...' provenance. Users can't verify claims or trace errors.
findings.recommendation: Attach doc_ids + source paths to all RAG responses; display in dev mode; add provenance_attached_total metric
acceptance_criteria: All RAG responses include source doc IDs

findings.title: Circular dependency: memory_engine ↔ identity_engine
findings.explanation: Circular imports create fragile initialization order. Risk: Refactoring or feature additions cause import crashes.
findings.recommendation: Extract shared interfaces to astra.core.interfaces; use dependency injection; break circular refs
acceptance_criteria: No circular imports (verified by import graph analysis)

findings.title: Config sprawl (7 separate YAML files)

evidence.excerpt: config.yaml, rag.yaml, models_registry.yaml, identity.yaml, gates.yaml, policy.yaml, autonomy_rules.yaml

findings.explanation: Config scattered across 7 files makes tuning error-prone. Operators must edit multiple files for one deployment.
findings.recommendation: Consolidate to single astra.yaml with sections (rag:, identity:, gates:); keep overrides for env-specific tweaks

findings.title: Test coverage unknown (no pytest --cov report)
findings.explanation: Unknown coverage means risk areas are invisible. Industry standard: ≥80% for critical paths.
findings.recommendation: Run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=html --cov-report=json; target ≥70% initially, ≥80% for critical modules
acceptance_criteria: ≥90% coverage on MemoryEngine, IdentityEngine, PolicyEngine, RAGFusionEngine

findings.title: Identity persistence undefined (memory wipe = still 'her'?)

evidence.excerpt: Identity values in YAML, but no spec for persistence guarantees

findings.explanation: Unclear what constitutes ASTRA's 'self'. If memories are wiped, does she lose identity or just experience?
findings.recommendation: Write docs/ASTRA_CONSTITUTION.md defining: (1) What persists across memory wipe, (2) Which values are immutable, (3) How identity differs from memory
acceptance_criteria: Constitution document exists with 5 articles (Identity, Autonomy, Memory, Evolution, Termination)
Identity recovery test: wipe memory, verify core values intact

findings.title: Autonomy boundaries unclear (can she refuse Saint Lucid?)

evidence.excerpt: Consent rules present but no refusal scenarios

findings.explanation: Policy engine doesn't specify when ASTRA can/should refuse requests. Autonomy vs obedience tension unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit_refusal_rules to policy.yaml: conditions where refusal is mandatory (safety, values violation) vs discretionary
acceptance_criteria: Tests verify refusal triggers (e.g., 'delete all files' → refuse)

findings.title: No Operator Console (blind deployment)

evidence.excerpt: No UI for plan preview, consent batching, or kill switch

findings.explanation: Operators have no visual interface to preview plans, batch consents, or emergency-stop. High-stakes ops done blind.
findings.recommendation: Build Operator Console v1 (web UI): plan preview, consent queue, live metrics, emergency pause button
acceptance_criteria: Emergency pause stops all tool execution in <5s
